text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service="sre-contractors" incident="prod-inference-503s" severity=critical. Summary: spike of 503s from inference cluster in us-west-2. Auto-escalation policy applied.
pagerduty-bot: Incident created -> https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345 (auto-notify). Current status: triggered -> escalated to schedule 'sre-contractors'.
Emma: wait — that service looks wrong. The prod inference service should route to 'prod-inference' not 'sre-contractors'. :eyes:
Raj: confirmed, I just checked the routing matrix. There was a recent change to composite schedule bindings yesterday that may have clobbered a mapping.
Mike: timeline? did the first alert happen before or after the schedule change?
Raj: schedule change merged at 10:03 UTC per terraform deploy logs. PagerDuty events started at 10:12 UTC (see incident-bot).
Liz: customers reported elevated 503s starting ~10:10. Looks like PD routed the pages to contractors instead of the prod oncall. That explains delayed escalation to primary SRE.
Oncall-ops: I'm oncall now — contractors just got the page and acked, then realized they were not responsible and suppressed. We lost ~23 mins before the right team was reached.
Emma: can someone silence the noisy contractor pages while we fix routing? Use PD silence for the service.
Mike: doing now — `/pd-silence service:sre-contractors 30m` -> executed. :white_check_mark:
Raj: reproducing the bad mapping: the terraform var `pd_service_bindings` had an erroneous key. snippet: ```
# bad mapping snippet
pd_service_bindings = {
  "prod-inference" = ["prod-inference"]
  "sre-contractors" = ["prod-inference"] # <- accidental duplicate
}
```
Emma: ugh. So events for prod-inference were routed to both services because of the duplicate binding. Who pushed that?
Raj: was in PR #812 but merged by the infra bot during oncall. I guess the validation didn't catch overlapping bindings. I'll revert the binding now and open a fix PR to add a validation check.
Liz: in the short term we should rebind the active incident to the correct service so the primary oncall gets the notifications. Can someone reassign in PD UI?
Mike: I reassigned PD12345 to service `prod-inference` and re-annotated the incident. Notifying primary.
incident-bot: Incident update: assignment changed to service="prod-inference" assignee="Emma" (manual).
Emma: ack. Taking lead. Quick mitigation: rolling restart of inference worker pool on us-west-2 and monitoring error rate.
Oncall-ops: restart started at 10:36 UTC. Error rate falling. customer-facing 503s peaked at ~3.8% and returned to baseline by 10:45.
Liz: customer impact summary for now: ~23m of elevated 503s affecting ~12% of traffic in the affected shard; estimated customer-facing rate peaked 3.8%. We'll need to include this in the postmortem.
Raj: action items: (1) revert terraform binding (in flight) (2) add CI validation for duplicate bindings (3) postmortem and timeline (Emma to write) (4) add PD runbook step to confirm service mapping on merge.
Emma: I'll own the postmortem and the runbook update. Target draft by EOD.
Mike: also adding an alert to detect when PD ackers are from non-primary schedules (heuristic).
Liz: thumbs up. Thanks all for the quick mitigation. We'll reconvene in #postmortems after the doc. :thumbsup:
__notes: This document is a contiguous Slack thread string; messages are prefixed by sender name. No title included per agents.md.
